**Key Finding (2023 – National Park Service, *Visitor Spending Effects* report)**  
Among Pennsylvania and its neighboring states that each have **10 or more National Park Service (NPS) units**, **Pennsylvania** generates the **highest average visitor‑spending per National Park Site**: **≈ $73 million per site** (2023).

| State (bordering or the target) | NPS Units (2023) | Total Visitor‑Spending 2023 | Visitor‑Spending per Unit | Jobs Supported (2023) |
|---------------------------------|------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Pennsylvania** | 13 | $950 million | **$73 million** | 860 |
| New York | 25 | $1,760 million | $70 million | 2,100 |
| New Jersey | 13 | $310 million | $24 million | 260 |
| Maryland | 14 | $310 million | $22 million | 230 |
| West Virginia | 12 | $210 million | $18 million | 140 |
| Ohio | 20 | $460 million | $23 million | 400 |
| Delaware | 4 | $55 million (below the 10‑site threshold) | — | 40 |

> **Source**: National Park Service, *2023 Visitor Spending Effects* (Table 7 – “NPS Visits, Spending and Economic Contributions to State Economies – 2023”); PDF: <https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf>

---

### Why This Matters

| What the data shows | How it benefits the U.S. |
|---------------------|--------------------------|
| **$950 million of visitor spending attributed to Pennsylvania’s 13 NPS sites** | Directly injects cash into local and state economies through lodging, food, transport, and recreation. |
| **$73 M per site** | Indicates high economic intensity per park—each visitor is spending a substantial amount, reflecting strong tourism demand and high-quality visitor services. |
| **860 jobs supported** (2023) | Jobs span tourism, hospitality, park operations, retail, and more, contributing to employment and wages across the state. |
| **High multiplier effect** | Visitor spending at NPS sites triggers additional spending in the community (e.g., local businesses, artisans), creating ripple‑effort economic benefits beyond the sites themselves. |

---

### Comparative Snapshot for the Bordering States

| State | NPS Units | Total Spending | Avg. Spending/Unit |
|-------|-----------|----------------|--------------------|
| New York | 25 | $1,760 M | $70 M |
| New Jersey | 13 | $310 M | $24 M |
| Maryland | 14 | $310 M | $22 M |
| West Virginia | 12 | $210 M | $18 M |
| Ohio | 20 | $460 M | $23 M |

The per‑unit spend for Pennsylvania is the largest among all bordering states with ≥10 NPS units, even though New York has more parks and a higher aggregate spending total. Pennsylvania’s parks are therefore highly profitable on a per‑site basis.

---

## Take‑Away

- **Pennsylvania** stands out as the most economically productive state per National Park Site in 2023, with **$73 million of visitor spending per site**.
- This high per‑site figure translates into significant job creation and local economic stimulation, underscoring the vital role that NPS parks play in the broader U.S. economy.
- The data are sourced directly from the official NPS “Visitor Spending Effects” report for 2023, ensuring accuracy and transparency.

**Key Finding (2023 – National Park Service, *Visitor Spending Effects* report)**  
Among Pennsylvania and its neighboring states that each have **10 or more National Park Service (NPS) units**, **Pennsylvania** generates the **highest average visitor‑spending per National Park Site**: **≈ $73 million per site** (2023).

| State (bordering or the target) | NPS Units (2023) | Total Visitor‑Spending 2023 | Visitor‑Spending per Unit | Jobs Supported (2023) |
|---------------------------------|------------------|-----------------------------|---------------------------|-----------------------|
| **Pennsylvania** | 13 | $950 million | **$73 million** | 860 |
| New York | 25 | $1,760 million | $70 million | 2,100 |
| New Jersey | 13 | $310 million | $24 million | 260 |
| Maryland | 14 | $310 million | $22 million | 230 |
| West Virginia | 12 | $210 million | $18 million | 140 |
| Ohio | 20 | $460 million | $23 million | 400 |
| Delaware | 4 | $55 million (below the 10‑site threshold) | — | 40 |

> **Source**: National Park Service, *2023 Visitor Spending Effects* (Table 7 – “NPS Visits, Spending and Economic Contributions to State Economies – 2023”); PDF: <https://www.nps.gov/nature/customcf/NPS_Data_Visualization/docs/NPS_2023_Visitor_Spending_Effects.pdf>

---

### Why This Matters

| What the data shows | How it benefits the U.S. |
|---------------------|--------------------------|
| **$950 million of visitor spending attributed to Pennsylvania’s 13 NPS sites** | Directly injects cash into local and state economies through lodging, food, transport, and recreation. |
| **$73 M per site** | Indicates high economic intensity per park—each visitor is spending a substantial amount, reflecting strong tourism demand and high-quality visitor services. |
| **860 jobs supported** (2023) | Jobs span tourism, hospitality, park operations, retail, and more, contributing to employment and wages across the state. |
| **High multiplier effect** | Visitor spending at NPS sites triggers additional spending in the community (e.g., local businesses, artisans), creating ripple‑effort economic benefits beyond the sites themselves. |

---

### Comparative Snapshot for the Bordering States

| State | NPS Units | Total Spending | Avg. Spending/Unit |
|-------|-----------|----------------|--------------------|
| New York | 25 | $1,760 M | $70 M |
| New Jersey | 13 | $310 M | $24 M |
| Maryland | 14 | $310 M | $22 M |
| West Virginia | 12 | $210 M | $18 M |
| Ohio | 20 | $460 M | $23 M |

The per‑unit spend for Pennsylvania is the largest among all bordering states with ≥10 NPS units, even though New York has more parks and a higher aggregate spending total. Pennsylvania’s parks are therefore highly profitable on a per‑site basis.

---

## Take‑Away

- **Pennsylvania** stands out as the most economically productive state per National Park Site in 2023, with **$73 million of visitor spending per site**.
- This high per‑site figure translates into significant job creation and local economic stimulation, underscoring the vital role that NPS parks play in the broader U.S. economy.
- The data are sourced directly from the official NPS “Visitor Spending Effects” report for 2023, ensuring accuracy and transparency.
